While marked as non-market sensitive, substantial holder notices can act as a technical catalyst — increased concentrated ownership can reduce free float, tighten liquidity, and historically precede further accumulation or M&A activity in small-cap ASX names.

Kaolin is a high-value industrial mineral with growing demand in ceramics, paper, and emerging battery/EV applications; positive metallurgical characteristics (brightness, particle size, low impurities) could underpin a premium pricing narrative and attract offtake interest from downstream processors.

As a market-sensitive disclosure, the next catalysts to watch are full testwork results, independent resource estimation, and any indication of processing pathway (wet vs. dry beneficiation) — each of which will be key valuation inflection points for institutional due diligence.

With market-sensitive classification, the market will scrutinise drill hole assay data closely; if intercepts extend or improve upon prior results, XPD is well-positioned to accelerate resource definition drilling and attract strategic or major-company interest in the asset.

The immediate catalyst to watch is the nature and scale of the systematic program (geophysics, soil sampling, or drilling) and whether RMX discloses a defined work budget; absence of a capital raise alongside this announcement suggests existing cash is sufficient for near-term exploration, though investors should monitor the next quarterly for burn rate and program milestones.

RC splitting methodology adds analytical rigour by providing a second assay pass on existing drill core, meaning this result carries enhanced geological confidence without incremental drilling cost — a capital-efficient validation of Viking's grade profile.

Near-term catalysts to watch include follow-up infill or extensional drilling to test the continuity of this high-grade zone along strike and at depth, which could drive a resource upgrade and re-rating if additional intercepts confirm a coherent high-grade corridor.
